open_points.subject: A13 rule 6 confirmation binding
open_points.text: so that two different tuples never share an encoding and digest equality stands for equality of what was shown
open_points.question: Can digest collisions occur, and if they can, must a submission with different values but the same digest be refused or is that case outside the guarantee?
options: Restore the previous rule that digest collisions are outside the guarantee.
Require every differing submission to be refused, which requires retaining or otherwise comparing enough information beyond this digest.
Adopt an explicit ideal collision-free digest abstraction rather than claiming this property of a collision-resistant cryptographic digest.
open_points.default_guess: Restore the collision exception: require an injective encoding and a collision-resistant digest, but place equal-digest collisions outside the guarantee.

witness.initial: A session holds a pending confirmation represented only by the digest of tuple T1; a distinct tuple T2 has the same digest.
events: The owner is shown and receives the confirmation value for T1.
The owner submits T2 with that confirmation value.
Registry compares the submitted digest with the retained digest; the original values were never retained.
outcomes: The submission is refused because its action, target, version or inputs differ from what was shown.
The submission passes the binding check because the only retained values, the digests, are equal.
witness.observer: The owner and the store observe whether the confirmed action is refused or applied.

open_points.subject: A21 review of the A13 change
open_points.text: no right, limit, class or answer moved, and no outcome changed.
open_points.question: Did the review intentionally change the collision case from outside the guarantee to a mandatory refusal, or must A13 retain the former exception so that this no-outcome-change statement is true?
options: Keep the new mandatory-refusal guarantee and state that the collision-case outcome changed.
Restore the collision exception and retain the statement that no outcome changed.
open_points.default_guess: Restore the collision exception and retain the no-outcome-change conclusion.

witness.initial: Two distinct confirmation tuples have the same cryptographic digest.
events: A confirmation is shown for the first tuple.
A submission carries the same confirmation value with the second tuple.
outcomes: Under the former text, the collision is outside the guarantee.
Under the changed A13 text, the submission is guaranteed to be refused.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether Registry promises a refusal in this history.

open_points.subject: confirmation digest algorithm
open_points.text: the digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest
open_points.question: Which cryptographic digest algorithm and output representation will generated code use?
options: SHA-256 with a fixed textual encoding.
Another fixed, supported collision-resistant digest with an explicitly fixed representation.
open_points.default_guess: Use SHA-256 and retain fixed-length raw bytes internally.
consequences: The choice determines digest length, stored representation, dependency/API use and compatibility across generated modules.
Changing it later can invalidate pending confirmations or require versioning if representations cross a process or release boundary.
open_points.requirement: the digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest

open_points.subject: confirmation tuple encoding
open_points.text: one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one
open_points.question: Which concrete canonical encoding will generated code use for this tuple?
options: A canonical length-prefixed binary encoding with explicit type and absence tags.
A canonical structured encoding with fixed field order, explicit nulls and deterministic list ordering.
A dedicated typed encoder whose injectivity is checked by Factory tests.
open_points.default_guess: Use a length-prefixed binary encoding with explicit type, field and absence tags.
consequences: The choice determines how type boundaries, nested lists, text encoding and absent values are represented.
Different choices remain valid only if they are injective for all admissible tuples and every producer and verifier uses the same encoding.
open_points.requirement: one unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from an empty one
